item.title: Trump and Xi's Empty Summit Is Straight Out of the 1930s
item.description: If the volume and glitter of the pageantry were a good indicator, the relationship between the United States and China would seem to be in great shape. Alas, summitry without substance can also be a harbinger of great danger, as the history of the 1930s teaches.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Kluth

item.title: Threats of Annihilation Are More Than Just Rhetoric
item.description: Leaders use fighting words at everyone’s risk.
item.dc:creator: Howard Chua-Eoan

item.title: The EU Faces Big Risks in Following the China Model
item.description: The political scientist Samuel Lubell once argued that America’s two political parties could be divided into the “party of the sun” which sets the national agenda and the party of the moon which merely reflects that agenda. The party of the sun changed from the Democrats in 1945-1980 to the Republicans from 1980 onward.
item.dc:creator: Adrian Wooldridge

item.title: The Big One Is Rumbling in the Bond Market
item.description: There are shifts underway, but for now the ground remains stable.
item.dc:creator: John Authers

item.title: Child Tax Credit Offers a Better Solution Than Vance’s Child Care Proposal
item.description: The White House is considering a plan to allow married, stay-at-home parents to be paid through the Child Care and Development Block Grant (CCDBG), a child-care fund for impoverished working parents. But there are more generous ways to support at-home parents that are fiscally responsible and that don’t compromise resources for other families.
item.dc:creator: Abby McCloskey

item.title: AI and Crypto Money in the Midterms Is Par for Politics
item.description: The AI and cryptocurrency sectors are bankrolling hundreds of millions of dollars in advertising to shape public opinion and elect allies to Congress and key state offices in the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: David M. Drucker

item.title: Measles Is On the Rise. CDC Should Keep Its Data Consistent
item.description: Pennsylvania officials have confirmed four measles-related deaths. Two, according to reports, are children. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has been embroiled in a public battle of semantics over how to characterize the circumstances. To the rest of the nation, the debate obscures a more obvious problem. Measles — a highly contagious, vaccine-preventable and sometimes fatal disease — is on the rise.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: SpaceX’s Starship Ushers In an Era of More Junk in Orbit
item.description: As early as next week, the world will leave behind 69 years of space exploration and commerce and enter the age of Starship, an era that will be defined by drastically lower launch costs and a notable increase in the amount of material humans send to orbit.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Black

item.title: Higher Bond Yields Have Changed What Safety Means
item.description: At least once a year, regardless of market conditions, some investment bank or another announces that it is “redefining” investing. I remember attending a presentation way back in 2019 at which a senior banker argued that, after nearly a decade of low bond yields, the standard 60/40 portfolio (60% stocks, 40% bonds) needed to be rethought. After a long song and dance, his “redefinition” amounted to putting some riskier assets in the bond portfolio to goose returns.
item.dc:creator: Allison Schrager

item.title: SpaceX, Anthropic Listings Are Part of What Ails the IPO Market
item.description: The US may yet notch a record year in initial public offerings if Anthropic PBC goes public soon. But it would be a false dawn, the numbers flattered by the trading debuts of Space Exploration Technologies Corp. and the aforementioned maker of the Claude chatbot. Under the surface, America’s withered IPO market is crying out for revitalization following a decades-long structural shift toward private funding that’s curbed transparency and walled off access to the best investment opportunities.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Levin

item.title: Two Sides of Queen Elizabeth Are Captured in a Pair of $5,000 Enamels
item.description: The arrival of Swan Song: Diana, My Sister, Charles Spencer’s memoir of his late sibling, has engulfed British tabloids and the global celebrity press. item.dc:creator: Howard Chua-Eoan

item.title: Trump's Casual Threat of Annihilating Iran Ramps Up a Genuine Danger
item.description: Visiting mixed villages in former Yugoslavia before it careened toward its violent breakup in 1992, I spoke to neighbors who dismissed the idea of a coming war as simply unimaginable. But as each tuned in to the increasingly nationalistic TV stations of their respective Serbian or Croatian capitals, they were bombarded by commentary posing as news that recalled historical wrongs and alleged plots for coming atrocities. Steeped in these bilious alternative realties, the neighbors stopped talking.
item.dc:creator: Marc Champion

item.title: Hermes has options for addressing its Birkin bag crisis
item.description: It must have been hurtful for the house of Hermes when Emily Oberg, founder of cult label Sporty & Rich, which styles its streetwear with gold Cartier watches and 1980s Porsches, declared that carrying a regular leather Birkin was akin to toting a Coach bag.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Felsted

item.title: Putin’s Shadow War Is Testing NATO’s Restraint
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin, frustrated by his bogged-down war in Ukraine, is trying to intimidate the European nations that — given President Donald Trump’s severe cuts in aid to Kyiv — are now Ukrainians’ main military, economic and diplomatic supporters.
item.dc:creator: James Stavridis
